name: Compositional Balance: Using Visual Weight with Purpose
description: Learn how compositional balance uses visual weight, symmetry, asymmetry, space and optional grids to create stability, tension and purposeful photographs.

step.name: Choose a scene where one area, relationship or pattern attracts your attention.
step.text: Choose a scene where one area, relationship or pattern attracts your attention. State what interests you.

step.name: Make one version that feels relatively settled.
step.text: Make one version that feels relatively settled. You might use symmetry, a central relationship or a more even distribution of visual weight.

step.name: Make another version that allows more dominance, asymmetry or tension.
step.text: Make another version that allows more dominance, asymmetry or tension. Change your position or framing while keeping other choices as similar as practical.

step.name: Check the frame edges, the surrounding space and where attention falls.
step.text: Check the frame edges, the surrounding space and where attention falls. Briefly squint to notice broad tonal weight, then look normally again to restore detail and meaning.

step.name: Compare the two photographs without an overlay.
step.text: Compare the two photographs without an overlay. Explain which version better supports your intention and identify one visible reason.
